People say I’m always moving—tapping my foot, gesturing while I talk. I don’t mean to, but it’s like I can’t sit still. I catch myself talking a lot too, even when others seem overwhelmed. Sometimes, in between movements of a piece, I hear voices calling my name—just faint, like an echo in an empty hall—but no one else hears it. It scares me, but it’s not constant. I don’t know if it’s stress, if I’m just overstimulated, or if something deeper is happening. I just feel... unmoored.

    D. Adjustment Disorder

D001-D005_h021.question:
I’ve been struggling for a while now—hard to say exactly how long, maybe a year or so, give or take. Lately, I’ll be driving my truck and suddenly realize I missed an exit or messed up the delivery instructions. I used to be sharp with those details. My wife’s been on me about chores at home too—she’ll ask me to fix something, I start, then get distracted and never finish. I can’t explain it.  

I feel like I’m always moving—can’t sit still, even when I’m off the road. My mind races, and sometimes I’ll jump into conversations at the truck stop before people are done talking. I don’t mean to, it just happens.  

And… look, this is hard to say—but sometimes I hear things. Like someone whispering my name when no one’s there. Once, I thought I saw shadows moving in the cab when I was alone. I know how that sounds. It’s not constant, just… now and then. I don’t know if it’s stress, lack of sleep, or something else. The thoughts don’t hang around long enough to make sense of, and I wouldn’t say I’ve been seeing things all the time. I just feel scattered—like I can’t keep up with myself.
D001-D005_h021.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D001-D005_h021.answer: B & A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D001-D005_h022.question:
I’ve been struggling for a while—maybe the past few months, though looking back, some things might’ve been off for longer. At work, I’m an insurance agent, so staying focused on policy details is crucial, but lately I keep missing small print, double-checking clients’ forms three times only to realize I skipped a section. I start on a task, get distracted by a phone alert or a coworker walking by, and then I’m sidetracked. I never used to be like this.

I’ve also felt restless—like I can’t sit still during meetings, even though I know I should. My leg bounces, I tap my pen, and sometimes I’ll jump in to answer before someone’s finished explaining. I’ve interrupted my boss mid-sentence more than once. I know it’s rude, but it’s like the thought’s out before I can stop it.

And recently… I can’t be sure, but sometimes I think people are talking about me when they’re not. I’ll hear my name in a conversation and turn, but it wasn’t me. Or I get this sense someone’s watching, but there’s no one there. It’s fleeting—like a shadow. I don’t know if it’s stress, lack of sleep, or something more.
D001-D005_h022.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D001-D005_h022.answer: B & A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D001-D005_h023.question:
I’ve been struggling lately—like, really struggling. My mind feels all over the place. I’ll sit down to finish a painting for class, and I start okay, but then little things distract me: the sound of someone walking by, a flickering light, even my own thoughts just… jump. I end up making these careless mistakes—like mixing up colors I know by heart, or skipping steps. It’s frustrating because I care, but I can’t seem to stay on track. I’ll start a project and never finish it, even when I want to.

People say I’m always moving—fidgeting, pacing, tapping. I don’t mean to interrupt, but sometimes I just blurt things out in class or cut someone off mid-sentence because the thought feels urgent, like if I don’t say it now, I’ll lose it. And… sometimes thoughts come that don’t feel entirely mine. Like, I’ll hear my name whispered when no one’s there, or think someone’s watching my work too closely—reading my mind. I can’t tell what’s real half the time. I don’t know how long this has been going on. Feels like a few months? Maybe longer. It’s all blurring together.
D001-D005_h023.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D001-D005_h023.answer: B & A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D001-D005_h024.question:
I’ve been struggling to keep up with my work lately—my sewing, which used to be so precise, now has mistakes I don’t even notice until the customer points them out. I’ll start altering a suit, get halfway through, then realize I’ve forgotten the instructions they gave me. It’s frustrating because I’ve always prided myself on my attention to detail. I try to focus, but my mind just… drifts.  

Lately, I feel restless, like I can’t sit still even when I need to thread a needle. My hands are always moving, I’m pacing between fittings, and sometimes I’ll jump into helping another client before finishing the one I’m with. My assistant mentioned I cut her off mid-sentence yesterday—I didn’t even realize I did it.  

And… well, sometimes I hear my late husband’s voice, just faintly, like a whisper when no one’s there. Or I feel like people are watching me through the shop window, studying my movements. I can’t tell if it’s grief or something else. I don’t know when all this really started—months, maybe? It’s all just… blended together.
D001-D005_h024.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D001-D005_h024.answer: B & A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D001-D005_h025.question:
I’ve been struggling at work lately—just can’t seem to stay focused, even though I’ve done this job for over ten years. Up in the crane, you need sharp attention, but I’ve caught myself zoning out or missing small details, like misreading signals. Made a few close calls. My foreman’s noticed. I don’t make mistakes like that usually, but recently… I start tasks, but sometimes don’t finish them. Like yesterday—I was supposed to double-check the rigging after my shift, but got distracted and just left it. No excuse.  

My wife says I’m restless, like I can’t sit still. I pace the house, flick through channels, can’t settle. Sometimes I jump into conversations, cut her off—I don’t mean to, it’s just the words come out fast. Truth is, I’ve been hearing things too. Voices muttering when no one’s around, like someone’s just out of sight. I don’t know if they’re real or if I’m tired. I can’t tell when it started—maybe months? It’s not constant.  

I’m scared, yeah. But I don’t know if this is stress, something mental, or just fatigue from being on my feet all day. Nothing’s been like this before, and I can’t figure out what’s what.
D001-D005_h025.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D001-D005_h025.answer: B & A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Schizophrenia
